records.researcher_notes: Latest Activity is a date field, so it records when the project was last reported on. The newest dated report found is a Riverhead Local article from April 8, 2025. It says a Department of Energy request for information, issued that week for an AI data center at Brookhaven National Laboratory, points to the Caithness site as the possible location of a new 750 MW gas turbine plant. The same article says Caithness 2 had been sidelined earlier when the Long Island Power Authority and PSEG Long Island decided it was not needed. An older TBR News Media article from July 9, 2018 reports that Caithness asked the Brookhaven town board on June 26, 2018 to allow a smaller 600 MW plant. The status stays announced. No start date and no turbine make or model were found.

records.researcher_notes: The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists Astoria Generating Station, plant 8906, generator 4, in its retired sheet. It shows a nameplate of 387.0 MW, an operating date of December 1961, and a retirement date of February 2021. GEM has this unit as mothballed. That is a status change, and I found only this one publisher. The New York Independent System Operator and the plant owner did not give a second document that I could open. The federal table says this unit retired in February 2021, not mothballed. I could not find a second publisher, so the change is medium confidence. I found no mothball notice for unit 4.

records.researcher_notes: On September 15, 2022, NRG and Beacon Wind asked the New York Public Service Commission to approve the sale of the land under the Astoria peaker plant. An Earthjustice press release from September 16, 2022 says approval would end NRG's appeal of the Title V air permit denial and its replacement plant. A New York Lawyers for the Public Interest case page says NRG applied to withdraw from the permit process on September 15. So the project was dropped in 2022. The appeal ended through NRG's September 2022 request to withdraw, tied to the land sale. No separate dismissal order was found. GEM already shows 2021 here. The sources above point to 2022, so this edit changes it. Check them before entering.
